title: Article 200: Governor's assent to state bills
body: When a state legislature passes a bill, the Governor may assent, withhold assent, return it (if not a Money Bill) for reconsideration, or reserve it for the President. If the House passes a returned bill again, the Governor cannot withhold assent. The text sets no deadline. Article 201 covers bills reserved for the President.

title: Article 111: President's assent to Union bills
body: The President may assent to or withhold assent from a bill passed by Parliament, or return a non-Money Bill once for reconsideration. If Parliament passes it again, the President must assent. This is the Union counterpart of Article 200.

title: Article 110: Money Bills
body: Defines a Money Bill as one dealing only with matters such as taxes, borrowing, the Consolidated Fund and appropriations. It can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha; the Rajya Sabha can only recommend changes within 14 days. The Speaker certifies whether a bill is a Money Bill.

title: Article 21: Protection of life and personal liberty
body: No person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except by procedure established by law. Courts have read it widely since Maneka Gandhi (1978) to include dignity, privacy (Puttaswamy, 2017), a clean environment, livelihood and speedy trial. Article 21A adds the right to education for ages 6 to 14.

title: Article 356: President's Rule
body: If the President is satisfied that a state's government cannot be carried on as per the Constitution, the Union can take over its executive functions. Parliament must approve within two months. S. R. Bommai (1994) made the proclamation open to judicial review and set the floor test as the way to check majority.

title: Sarkaria Commission (1983–88)
body: Reviewed Centre–state relations. Recommended that Governors be eminent persons from outside the state and not active politicians, that Article 356 be used sparingly as a last resort, and that an Inter-State Council be set up under Article 263 (created in 1990).

title: Punchhi Commission (2007–10)
body: Second review of Centre–state relations. Suggested fixed tenure for Governors, removal only by a state legislature resolution process, a time limit for decisions on state bills, and localising emergency provisions to districts where possible.

title: Monetary Policy Committee and inflation targeting
body: The RBI Act, 1934 was amended in 2016 to set up a six-member MPC (three from the RBI including the Governor, three external). The government sets the CPI inflation target, currently 4 percent with a band of 2 to 6 percent. The MPC sets the repo rate, the rate at which the RBI lends to banks overnight.

title: Disaster Management Act, 2005
body: Created the NDMA (chaired by the Prime Minister), State DMAs (chaired by Chief Ministers), District DMAs and the NDRF. Marked India's shift from relief after disasters to preparedness, mitigation and early warning. India follows the Sendai Framework 2015–2030.

title: Cooperative federalism
body: The Union and states working together rather than in competition. Institutions include the Inter-State Council, the GST Council (a model of shared decision-making), NITI Aayog's Governing Council and zonal councils. Friction points include the Governor's role, fiscal transfers and Article 356.

title: Right to Information Act, 2005
body: Lets citizens request information from public authorities, with replies due in 30 days (48 hours where life or liberty is involved). Information Commissions hear appeals. Section 8 lists exemptions. The 2019 amendment let the Union set commissioners' tenure and pay.

title: Ramsar Convention on Wetlands
body: Signed in 1971 at Ramsar, Iran, to conserve wetlands of international importance. India joined in 1982 and has more than 80 Ramsar sites. The Montreux Record lists sites under threat. Wetlands help with flood control, groundwater recharge and livelihoods.
